subject: Price-model readiness + QA plan for MAP / evaluation

From: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.ai>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-12-02T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Price-model readiness + QA plan for MAP / evaluation

Claire — following up from yesterday's sync. I put together a compact MAP-focused checklist that ties the mutual action plan milestones to the unit-econ checks we discussed. Attached: redwood_MAP_draft.xlsx and a first-pass token_cost_model_v1.csv (internal assumptions).

High-level asks from Aurelia to help finalize economics and the evaluation plan:
- Projected steady-state QPS during business hours and expected peak QPS (one number each)
- Typical input (prompt) token distribution: median and 90th percentile for the first-week prompts, plus average generation length if any
- Any nonstandard system prompts / long few-shot contexts we should treat as cacheable prefixes
- Procurement & legal target close date (we'd like to align POC gating with that)

Proposed Redwood assumptions (we'll validate with load runs in the POC):
- Baseline model variant: small-medium open model (latency target p95 < 350ms) with a nominal hosted unit cost we list in the CSV.
- Batching: conservative working assumption = 12-16 effective parallel requests per GPU under your latency SLO; expect ~15% token-cost savings at 16 rps batching compared to single-request footing.
- Prefix/KV caching: system prompts + static few-shot examples estimated to reduce billed prompt tokens by ~30-40% for common flows (we'll measure).
- Quality vs cost: evaluation plan will include a head-to-head run of two model/quantization profiles so we can show delta in latency and token $/1k requests.

Suggested timeline (flexible):
- Dec 7: POC kickoff (environment + credentials + test corpus)
- Dec 8–14: Instrumentation + smoke runs; capture sample traffic and tune batching/caching knobs
- Dec 15–22: Full evaluation week(s) with seeded prompts, perf and quality metrics, and token cost reconciliation
- Jan 10–15: Procurement/contract close (target)

Action items / owners:
- Claire / Aurelia: send forecast + sample prompt corpus (due Dec 5)
- Marissa: validate deployment options and SLA notes for MAP document (I'll loop her into the POC kickoff)
- Ben: prepare the cost model variant table and latency knobs to test (I attached the first-pass CSV)

If this looks okay I can lock the MAP file and the test harness and schedule the kickoff.

Thanks,
Diego Fernandez
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
Mobile: +1 (415) 555-0198

Attachments: redwood_MAP_draft.xlsx (xlsx), token_cost_model_v1.csv (csv)

Subject: Re: Price-model readiness + QA plan for MAP / evaluation

Claire — great, thanks for the forecast and the prompt samples. I've updated the MAP draft to reflect the burst numbers and the 600-token system prompt (we'll treat it as a cacheable prefix in the POC unless you tell us otherwise). A few clarifications and the explicit acceptance criteria proposal below.

SLA / capacity notes:
- For sustained peaks above committed capacity, we offer a staged escalation: automated autoscale within Dedicated pool (if customer has Dedicated), short-term burst credits (up to X hours) and a documented SLA-credit process for repeated violations. We'll surface the precise wording in the contract redlines.

Unit-econ acceptance criteria (proposal to include in MAP):
- Measurement window: 7-day rolling evaluation during POC window.
- Baseline metric: median tokens/$ per 1k successful requests (excludes retries) measured on identical prompt set.
- Target: < $0.75 per 1k requests (this is illustrative; Ben's cost-model variants will show exact deltas across model/quant profiles).
- Batching/caching gates: must demonstrate at least 15% reduction in billed tokens or equivalent CPU/GPU-hour reduction when caching is enabled for the static prefixes, and measurable batching improvements at 16-request concurrency.

Evaluation plan (concrete):
1) Data & access (Dec 7): Aurelia provides sample corpus + test credentials. Redwood instruments a staging route that mirrors production routing and logs token-level breakdown per request.
2) Smoke & calibration (Dec 8–9): run small load tests to calibrate batching window and effective concurrency to meet latency p95 targets.
3) Full-run (Dec 10–16): run three full passes over seed prompts at target concurrency and collect: tokens/request (prompt vs generation), p50/p95 latency, total billed tokens, and model output quality samples.
4) Quality gating (Dec 17–19): Aurelia product team reviews blind sample of outputs for regression vs your baseline; we capture pass/fail and rubric scores.
5) Final reconciliation (Dec 20–22): produce final tokens/$ for MAP and sign-off document.

Notes on our internal assumptions (from token_cost_model_v1.csv):
- Nominal cost basis: modeled on GPU-hour + infra amortization; we show effective $ per 1M tokens across two model variants.
- Quantization: we will test a 4-bit quantized variant (smaller memory footprint) and a higher-accuracy FP16 variant; expect tradeoffs: ~18–28% lower compute cost with quant but 2–5% quality delta (to be measured).
- Caching effect: caching only reduces billed prompt tokens; generation tokens remain the same. For flows where the system prompt + few-shot represents >50% of prompt tokens, caching provides outsized savings.

Mutual action list (owner — due):
- Aurelia: provide anonymized prompt set + forecast (Claire) — Due Dec 5
- Redwood: instantiate POC staging route + instrumentation (Marissa) — Due Dec 7
- Redwood: run calibration + full runs; produce tokens/$ reconciliation (Ben + Priyom) — Dec 10–22
- Both: QA review and acceptance decision (Aurelia product + Redwood CS) — Complete by Dec 22

I'll kick off a calendar invite for Dec 7 once Marissa confirms environment readiness. If Aurelia needs the caching behavior disabled for regulatory reasons we can measure both on/off during runs.

Diego
